solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit and nut trees're possibly obstacles for pedestrians

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the three fodder words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A woodland walker finds fruit and nut trees blocking the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a joining word; the anagram signalled by 'possibly' uses FRUIT, NUT and TREES'RE, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollards, benches, lamp posts and bins are the kerbside fittings walkers have to step round, collectively called by this phrase.

clue.text: To demonstrate contentment, the thing is getting up and mounting support

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters climb, so the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cat purrs to show it is content
the thing is = it is, shortened to it's (ITS)

explanation.surface: A contented cat purrs while something is climbing up onto a support.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'getting up' reads the whole run upwards; 'the thing is' contracts to it's, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rests in this loop when climbing onto a horse, so it supports the act of mounting.

clue.text: Vermin killer trapping large viper

indicators.note: trapping means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a ratter is a dog or cat that kills rats
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A terrier that hunts vermin corners a big snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a pit viper, and this is its informal name.

clue.text: Alternate with saints working to protect male one and all

indicators.note: to protect means the preceding letters surround and shield the next piece

parts.note: alternate, as in every other day
S is the abbreviation for saint, so SS for saints
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: Taking turns with holy figures on duty guarding a man.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means absolutely everybody, every single person without exception.

clue.text: Fashion of the sort cutting husband's 1 Down, say

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape or make, so the letters are reworked
cutting means a piece is removed from the words

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A style of the kind that trims a husband's stirrup, as a sort of example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' removes H from OF THE SORT, leaving OFTESORT, which 'Fashion' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup (the answer to 1 Down) is one example of something a rider's foot is placed on.

clue.text: Spirit of Mediterranean's hot and dissipated

parts.note: raki is an aniseed spirit of Turkey and the eastern Mediterranean, plus the 's
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean liquor is fiery and leaves drinkers debauched.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a dashing but dissolute, loose-living character.

clue.text: Venus and Mercury gather the brute's eating men, even

parts.note: to gather is to deduce or infer

indicators.note: eating means taking letters inside, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: a brute animal is an 'it', so the brute's is ITS
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers
plane means flat or level, as even does

explanation.surface: Two gods conclude that a beast is devouring people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' signals containment; 'men' as OR (other ranks) and 'even' as the adjective plane (level) are the hard steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers give this name to the two worlds orbiting closer to the Sun than Earth does.

clue.text: Purged a faulty replacement of equipment

indicators.note: faulty says the letters of the words are flawed and must be put right

explanation.surface: Faulty machines were cleared out and swapped for new kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvement swapping old hardware for newer, better kit is called this.

clue.text: European engaged in initiative is to take a hit

parts.note: at means busy with, as in 'at work'
taking the lead is showing initiative

explanation.surface: A European getting involved in a scheme ends up suffering a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang from gangster films: to be shot, struck by bullets.

clue.text: Where to find nettle sting relief being tried?

definitions.text: Where to find nettle sting relief
definitions.meaning: rubbing a dock leaf on the skin is the folk remedy for a nettle sting
standing trial in court, in the defendant's enclosure

explanation.surface: A herbal-remedy question that also hints at a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The defendant's box in a criminal court is the dock, and dock leaves grow beside nettles.

clue.text: Scrap of fruit before empty harvest

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

indicators.note: empty means the middle letters are removed, leaving only the outside ones

explanation.surface: A morsel of fruit ahead of a poor harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a small piece of fruit, but here it is the verb or noun for a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a brawl or scuffle.

clue.text: Recuperate, indeed deficient in energy

indicators.note: deficient in means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: really and indeed are both interjections of emphasis
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A patient recovers, though indeed short of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover strength after illness or a setback; synonyms in the sense of picking up.

clue.text: At last, some waves in trough become evident again

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a race is a channel, like a mill race, as a trough is

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: surf is breaking waves

explanation.surface: Eventually some waves form within a trough of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' applies to 'some' alone; 'in' is the container signal, and a race is a fast channel of water such as a mill race.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back up to the surface, or figuratively reappear, as a problem does.

clue.text: Streamlined swimmer's defective equilibrium giving nothing away

indicators.note: giving ... away means a letter is surrendered from the words
away completes giving ... away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: poor means inferior or defective
O looks like zero, nothing
poise is balance or equilibrium

explanation.surface: A sleek sea creature has lost its balance but gives nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving nothing away' removes one O from POOR + POISE.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea mammal, kin of the dolphin, has a sleek torpedo-shaped body.

clue.text: Sounded bullish when welcoming new budget?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so letters go inside

parts.note: cattle low, so a bull lowed

explanation.surface: A stock-market voice sounded optimistic about a new budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullish' suggests markets, but it means sounding like a bull; 'budget' is an adjective, as in budget airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap, bottom-of-the-range goods are described by this compound adjective.

clue.text: Maybe Racine swallows a round loaf like Jonson

indicators.note: swallows means taking something inside

parts.note: Jean Racine was the French dramatist, so Jean is one example of a first name
a cob is a round loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A French playwright eats a loaf, just as the English one Jonson might.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson wrote under King James I, the period this adjective describes.

clue.text: Going round D is among small accomplishments in pool

indicators.note: going round means one word encircles another

parts.note: with can mean among, as in 'with the crowd'

explanation.surface: A swimmer counts the short lengths done across a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers who cross a pool sideways cover its short dimension, these shorter laps.

clue.text: Stupid tricks succeeded, taking tons in

indicators.note: taking ... in means accepting a piece inside
in completes taking ... in, putting one piece within

parts.note: wiles are tricks or ruses
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Silly ruses worked, bringing in tons of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sense or brains; foolish.

clue.text: Furious, perhaps, having serving of cappuccino (medium) upended

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up
a serving of is a portion taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A furious diner knocks over a medium cappuccino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving of' picks CINOMED from the words; 'upended' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies were avenging spirits, so being like one is fiendish.

clue.text: Reverse hire purchase plan allowed in brochure

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the next words backwards

parts.note: a map is a plan
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A leaflet explaining how to undo a credit deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like part of a financial phrase, but it turns the next two pieces backwards together; hire purchase is the British term for buying on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A booklet or leaflet giving information, as a brochure does.

clue.text: Accepting reporting restriction, see no way back

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: accepting means taking a piece inside

parts.note: a gag is an order restricting what the press may report

explanation.surface: A journalist accepts a gag order and sees no route back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way back' looks like a route home but means in the distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase 'way back' means in times far in the past.

clue.text: Sci-fi fan lovelessly ripped edges of Kirk image

indicators.note: lovelessly means without love, the zero score in tennis written O

parts.note: tore means ripped

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A spurned fan tears the corners off a picture of Captain Kirk.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee of the Star Trek franchise, whose hero is Kirk.

clue.text: Irregularity in colouring mess, going over line

indicators.note: going over means one piece covers or surrounds another

parts.note: a botch is a mess

explanation.surface: A child's colouring-in is messed up by going over the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A patchy mark or stain, an uneven spot of colour on skin or paper.

clue.text: Cheers rider at front in Tour de France jersey, after cutting fruit

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as cheers is

indicators.note: in places a letter inside other letters
after cutting means the word has been trimmed at its tail

parts.note: the maillot jaune is the yellow jersey of the Tour de France

indicators.note: at front picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cheering crowd greets the leading rider in his Tour de France jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cutting' clips the jersey's last letter; 'in' then houses the rider's initial. The French maillot is any jersey, the yellow one going to the race leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree tomato is a red egg-shaped fruit from South America also known by this name.

clue.text: Regularly struck, wasn't noise musical?

indicators.note: regularly struck means every other letter is struck out

explanation.surface: A puzzled listener asks whether the regular beat was noise or music.
explanation.definitionFit: A Broadway musical about the comic-strip orphan, known for the song Tomorrow.

clue.text: Before marriage, British sportswoman not having the head for Wimbledon event?

indicators.note: not having the head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis championship

explanation.surface: A British athlete who would hate tennis at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Jessica Ennis, Olympic heptathlon champion in 2012, became Ennis-Hill when she married; hence 'Before marriage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica Ennis is a British heptathlete; this was her surname before she married.

clue.text: What old-fashioned things are out of keeping Euro MP gives a place for topical amusement

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.words: What old-fashioned things are out of
parts.note: old-fashioned things are said to be 'out of the ark', Noah's ark
an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: An outdated politician offers a venue for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement park built round a single subject or topic, hence 'topical'.

clue.text: Reassign worker's donkey that's puffed, having already had a breather

definitions.text: that's puffed, having already had a breather

parts.note: to second a worker is to transfer them to other duties
a hand is a worker, plus the 's
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A boss transfers an employee's panting donkey after it had a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco smoke inhaled by others after the smoker has already breathed it, a breather being someone breathing it first.
